long_biography.plain_text:
Exchanging television channels for shares helped Vincent Bolloré establish a substantial position in French media. His group sold Direct 8 and Direct Star to Canal+ in 2012, receiving Vivendi shares and subsequently increasing its investment. Television ownership became part of a broader set of interests spanning music, publishing and advertising.

The separation of Vivendi’s businesses in 2024 left the family group with stakes in separately listed media companies, including Canal+ and Havas. Its large investment in Universal Music Group adds recorded music to that portfolio. Bolloré remains chairman and chief executive of Compagnie de l’Odet, the family holding company above Bolloré SE, whose chief executive is his son Cyrille.
